[engine] When a gate is changed from testing presence to testing value, re-derive the effective behaviour of EVERY configuration that set the variable, and restore the previous effective behaviour as the new default; verifying that one anchor digest is unchanged is not behavioural preservation, because the configurations that explicitly set the now-meaningful value are exactly the ones the fix cannot move.

<!-- generated by harness_engine/build_memories.py from traces/lessons.jsonl -->
<!-- lesson_id: eng-gate-0006 | class: gate-integrity | superseded_by: - -->

**class**: `gate-integrity`

## 為什麼（because）

CGC_OA_ASYNC was gated on `getenv(...) != nullptr` while run_server.sh unconditionally put the variable into SERVER_ENV, so the value was never read and every profile ran segmented -- including the four whose launcher default was 0. Making the gate value-aware at 21:36 therefore flipped off / prefill250 / qa-zh / longform-zh from segmented to non-segmented, i.e. from 6.95 t/s to 0.72 t/s in the same build (measured on the baseline arm pair, same md5, same pool counters). The anchor digest dc055e63 stayed identical throughout, and prod25 is precisely the one profile that sets the variable to 1 explicitly -- so the check that was run could not have detected the change it was standing in for. prefill250 is the profile the oracle gate and bench matrix run under, so the blast radius reached the verification chain.
